label: The 'as', or the 'a' right after me, us or you, when a label bounces back at me, us or you: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, calling, regarding, treating or describing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group label me, us or you in return, either with 'as' (they saw me as a fool) or bare with 'a' (he called me a liar). Weaker: the same two-way swap between named people or third-person pronouns. Weak: a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause; me labelled first and then answering back; a plural bare return with no 'as' or 'a' (named us cowards); a return aimed at a third party; official appointments to a post.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: The 'as' (or the 'a' just after it) when me, us or you is labelled back: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, thinking of, regarding, treating, describing or hailing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group see, think of, regard, treat, describe or hail me, us or you 'as' something in return; the return can end in a noun or an adjective. Weaker but can still fire: the same two-way mirror written entirely with third-person pronouns (he and her, they and him). Weak: mirrors between named people or noun phrases (the coach and the striker), a return clause aimed at a third person after an earlier clause about me, us or you, a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause, me labelled first and then answering back, the bare form without 'as' even inside a mirror (thinks me a fool), a return framed as what someone should do, and official appointments to a post.
